cases.question: What is the minimum number of inpatient beds required for a hospital to be empanelled under PM-JAY?
cases.answer:
The basic rule is that a hospital must have **at least 10 inpatient beds** (with the usual spacing and supporting staff) to be empaneled under PM‑JAY, although exemptions are allowed for single‑specialty facilities such as eye, ENT or standalone dialysis centres【1†L1-L4】【4†L1-L4】.  

For hospitals located in **Aspirational Districts**, the requirement is relaxed: they need **only 5 inpatient beds** (unless they are providing day‑care packages covered under PM‑JAY)【2†L1-L3】.

When is hospital empanelment due for renewal?

cases.question: By when should agency deploy team for the project?
cases.answer: The agency must deploy the project team **within fifteen (15) days of the date of signing the agreement or receiving the LOI**【3】.

cases.question: What is minimum experience and qualification required for data scientist role in agency?
cases.answer:
The agency requires a **Data Scientist / Analyst Consultant** to have:

* **Qualification:** A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics or a related field.  
* **Experience:** At least 5 years of experience in analytics and managing big data, **including a minimum of 3 years** developing AI/ML models, with demonstrable credentials of having built AI/ML models independently.  

[2]

cases.question: Will NHA make sure to answer every queries in pre-bid queries?
cases.answer: No. NHA says it will “endeavor to provide timely response to all the queries,” but it “makes no representation or warranty as to the completeness or accuracy of any response… nor does it undertake to answer all the queries that have been posed by the Bidders” [1].

cases.question: What is cut-off in technical evaluation for bidder?
cases.answer: The technical evaluation requires bidders to achieve a minimum score of **70 %**. The overall technical cut‑off is set at 70 % and bidders must obtain at least 70 % both in the aggregate technical score and in each individual section/sub‑section to qualify【1】. This requirement is reiterated in the evaluation rules, which state that bidders must “Attain an aggregate at least Technical Score of 70% or more” and also “Score at least 70% in individual sections and sub‑sections”【4】.

cases.question: What is timeline of empanelment request filed by hospital to DEC?
cases.answer: The District Empanelment Committee must finish its scrutiny and processing of a hospital’s empanelment request **within 15 days (15 working days) of receiving the application**【1†L1-L3】【3†L5-L7】.

cases.question: during inspection, if it is found that hospital has applied for multiple specialties, but all do not conform to minimum requirements under AB-PMJAY, then will it get empanelment?
cases.answer: If an inspection finds that a hospital has applied for multiple specialties and **none of those specialties meet the minimum requirements under AB‑PM‑JAY**, the hospital will **not be empanelled for all of them**. Instead, it will be empanelled **only for the specialties that do conform to AB‑PM‑JAY (or PM‑JAY) norms**; the non‑conforming specialties will not receive empanelment【1†23】【2†16】.

cases.question: How much incentive will hospital receive with full NABH accreditation?
cases.answer: A hospital that has **full NABH accreditation** receives a **15 % incentive** over the base procedure rate [1][3].

cases.question: Can proposal be disqualified in case of bidder increasing its quoted price after submission of the bid?

cases.answer: The guidelines require that **100 % of death (mortality) cases be audited by the State Health Agency (SHA)** as the minimum sample. [3][1]

cases.answer: ICU/Medical‑treatment blocking that lasts **more than 5 days** (when the patient does not have a critical illness) is listed as a fraud trigger. [3]

cases.question: What percentage of beneficiary audit needs to be at minimum?
cases.answer:
The sources give different minimum percentages for beneficiary audits:

* **Source [1]** lists the minimum sample for beneficiary audits as **10 % of total cases hospitalised** for audits conducted during hospitalisation and for post‑discharge telephone audits, and **5 % of total cases hospitalised** for post‑discharge home‑visit audits【1†L31-L38】.  

* **Source [3]** (and the same figure in **Source [4]**) states that the minimum sample for a beneficiary audit (at hospital or at home) is **3 % of total cases hospitalised**【3†L9-L13】【4†L9-L13】.  

Thus, the minimum percentage required for a beneficiary audit is reported as **10 %** in one source and **3 %** in two other sources.

cases.question: What is turn around time for SOS (Emergency) Grievances?
cases.answer: The prescribed turn‑around time for SOS (Emergency) grievances is **6 working hours**. If the case is not resolved within this time, the CEO of the State Health Agency is alerted via a system‑generated email【2】.

cases.question: Does desk Audit checklist contains need for ICU documents?

cases.question: If patient has received R-CHOP- and first cycle was given on 26 feb 2020 then how soon they can give approval of second cycle at max?
cases.answer:
The guidance states that the second R‑CHOP cycle should be given 21 days after the first cycle, but in case of a technical issue the approval may be issued **one day earlier** as an acceptable period【1】.  

- First cycle on 26 Feb 2020 → 21 days later is 18 Mar 2020.  
- The earliest (maximum‑soon) approval therefore can be given on **17 Mar 2020**.

cases.question: How can one raise grievance under AB PM-JAY using online mode?
cases.answer: A grievance can be raised online by logging onto the **Central Grievance Redressal Management System (CGRMS)** portal of AB PM‑JAY. The portal URL is https://cgrms.pmjay.gov.in (also shown as https://cgrms.pmjay.gov.in/GRMS/loginnew.htm) [1][2]. Through this online portal any stakeholder can register the complaint; the system automatically generates a **Unique Grievance Number (UGN)** and sends an SMS/email confirmation to the complainant [1][3].
